holidays.name: National Chocolate Cupcake Day
holidays.description: A day for peeling back the paper liner on a chocolate cupcake. Frosting is optional, but few people skip it. Bake a batch, buy one from a bakery, or bring a dozen to the office.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. It is part of the long run of dessert days that fill the calendar each October, which is also National Dessert Month.
holidays.funFact: The word 'cupcake' first appeared in print in 1796, in Amelia Simmons' 'American Cookery'. The name may come from the cups the batter was baked in.

holidays.name: National No Beard Day
holidays.description: A day for the clean-shaven. Beard owners are invited to trim it off, and everyone else can enjoy a smooth chin. Expect a lot of fresh faces and a few awkward pale patches.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is a playful counterpart to the many days that celebrate facial hair.
holidays.funFact: Peter the Great of Russia taxed beards in 1698. Men who kept theirs had to pay and carry a token to prove it.

holidays.name: National Necktie Day
holidays.description: A day to knot, loop and tighten that strip of fabric around your neck. It celebrates the necktie, a piece of clothing that is both stylish and slightly strangling. Dress up, and maybe show off your most outrageous tie.
holidays.origin: The day is tied to the necktie's roots in 17th-century Europe. Croatian soldiers wore knotted scarves, and the style caught on in France and then spread across the world. Croatia marks Cravat Day on the same date.
holidays.funFact: The word 'cravat' comes from 'Croat'. It is a nod to the Croatian mercenaries whose neckwear started the trend.
